newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AIG unit SPC Credit signs credit facility.
newsitem.headline: AIG unit SPC Credit signs credit facility.

text.p: SPC Credit Ltd has signed a HK$3.3 billion credit facility with 15 financial institutions, the coordinating arrangers said on Friday.
SPC Credit, which is wholly owned by American International Group Inc (AIG), currently is registered as a deposit taking company under the Hong Kong Banking Ordinance.
The facility was oversubscribed in syndication and increased to HK$3.3 billion from the original amount of HK$3.0 billion, the statement said.
The facility consists of a 364-day revolving credit and a three-year term loan.

The revolving credit is sub-divided into Tranche I of HK$1.1 billion and Tranche II of HK$550 million for both Hong Kong and U.S. dollar drawings, whereas the term loan of HK$1.65 billion is for Hong Kong dollar drawing.
Interest margins are 27 basis points per annum for the revolving credit facility and 40 basis points per annum for the term loan facility.
Proceeds of the facility will be used to refinance the company's HK$3.0 billion revolving credit facility due to mature in April 1997.
Arrangers and lead managers are Chase Manhattan Asia, Fuji Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, ABN AMRO Bank, BNP's Hong Kong branch, Sakura Bank, Sanwa Bank Hong Kong and Westdeutsche Landesbank.
Expanded lead managers are Asahi Bank's Hong Kong branch, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, National Australia Bank's Hong Kong branch and Rabobank's Hong Kong branch.
Co-lead managers are Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank's Hong Kong branch, Royal Bank of Canada and Tokai Bank's Hong Kong branch.
